title: Sentence Similarity II
constraints: sentence1[i] and sentence2[i] contain only English letters (upper or lower case)
xi and yi contain only English letters
signature: boolean areSentencesSimilarTwo(String[] sentence1, String[] sentence2, List<List<String>> similarPairs)
notes:
## Intuition

Because similarity is symmetric and transitive, the pairs split all words into groups: two words are similar exactly when a chain of pairs connects them. A brute force could search the pair graph (DFS or BFS) for every position, costing O(n · p). Union-find builds the groups once, after which each position needs only two near-constant `find` calls.

## Approach

1. Sentences of different lengths can never match, so return `false` right away.
2. Keep a map `parent` from each word to its parent; `find` adds unseen words as their own root and walks up to the root, halving the path as it goes.
3. For each pair `[first, second]`, find both roots and, if they differ, hang `rootA` under `rootB` to merge the groups.
4. For every index `i`, compare the roots of `sentence1[i]` and `sentence2[i]`; a mismatch means `false`.
5. If every position matched, return `true`.

## Example 1, step by step

The pairs link `great` under `good`, `fine` under `good`, `drama` under `acting` and `skills` under `talent`. At `i = 0`, `find("great")` and `find("fine")` are both `good`. At `i = 1`, `find("acting")` is `acting` and `find("drama")` is `acting`. At `i = 2`, both `skills` and `talent` lead to `talent`. Every position matches, so the answer is `true`.

## Complexity

- Time: O((n + p) · α) in practice (O(log) amortized with path halving alone): each pair and each position costs a couple of `find` calls.
- Space: O(p + n) for the `parent` map holding every distinct word.

## Pitfalls

- Check the lengths first; extra words on one side mean the sentences are not similar.
- A word that never appears in a pair is still similar to itself: `find` must register it as its own root rather than fail.
- Similarity is case-sensitive: `Great` and `great` are different words unless a pair links them.
- Merge roots, not the words themselves; setting `parent` of `first` directly can cut it off from its old group.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `parent` | map from each word to its parent in the union-find forest |
| `find` | returns the root word of a word's group, compressing the path |
| `first`, `second` | the two words of the current similar pair |
| `rootA`, `rootB` | roots of `first` and `second` before merging |
| `i` | index of the word pair being compared |
